vulns.title: SQL injection in /search (raw SQL built with %-formatting, run via db.engine.execute)
vulns.notes: request.json['search'] is %-formatted into str_query and passed to db.engine.execute() (line 265). JSON body param. Requires a valid JWT: POST /login {"username":"admin","password":"admin123"} returns the token in the Authorization response header; send it as Authorization on /search.

vulns.title: Reflected XSS / SSTI via render_template_string in the 404 handler (reflects request.url)
vulns.notes: UNCERTAIN detectability/classification: the 404 handler builds an HTML template with '%s' % request.url and passes it to render_template_string (line 114), so any unknown path reflects the URL unescaped (DAST-detectable as reflected XSS; it is also SSTI/CWE-94). SAST is unlikely to flag it: request.url is not in our taint-source list and render_template_string is not a standard sink. render_template_string is also reached in the /search error path (line 281) reflecting the 'search' term. No auth needed for the 404 path.

vulns.title: Hard-coded Flask secret_key
vulns.notes: app.secret_key assigned a literal string (session signing key). Code-only.

vulns.title: Hard-coded JWT HMAC signing key (SECRET_KEY_HMAC)
vulns.notes: app.config['SECRET_KEY_HMAC'] = 'secret' (literal); used to sign/verify JWTs at lines 86 and 184. A second literal key SECRET_KEY_HMAC_2 is on line 27. Code-only.

vulns.title: Missing security headers (no Content-Security-Policy, host-wide)
vulns.notes: UNCERTAIN runtime manifestation: a default Flask app sets no Content-Security-Policy (and no X-Frame-Options unless Flask-Talisman/manual), so responses are expected to lack CSP. Confirm the exact missing-header set against a live instance.
